intent.raw_query: Eastern Europe city hop Prague + Budapest, $1200, 8 days, September 2026

experiences.name: Prague Castle Complex Tour
experiences.description: Explore the largest ancient castle complex in the world, home to St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane. Walk through centuries of Bohemian history with stunning panoramic views of Prague's red-roofed skyline. A self-guided tour allows you to absorb the Gothic and Baroque architecture at your own pace.

experiences.name: Old Town Square & Astronomical Clock
experiences.description: Wander through Prague's medieval Old Town Square, anchored by the iconic 15th-century Astronomical Clock (Orloj). Watch the hourly mechanical show, admire the Gothic Týn Church, and soak in the vibrant street atmosphere. Climb the Old Town Hall tower for sweeping views over the historic center.

experiences.name: Budapest Buda Castle & Castle Hill Walk
experiences.description: Discover the UNESCO-listed Buda Castle district on foot, visiting the Hungarian National Gallery, Matthias Church, and the Fisherman's Bastion with its fairy-tale turrets. The hilltop location offers breathtaking views over the Danube River and the Pest skyline, making it one of the most photogenic spots in Central Europe.

experiences.name: Hungarian Parliament Building Guided Tour
experiences.description: Step inside one of Europe's most magnificent neo-Gothic buildings, the Hungarian Parliament, which dominates the Danube riverbank. A guided interior tour reveals the ornate Grand Staircase, the Holy Crown of Hungary, and lavishly decorated legislative chambers. The building's history mirrors Hungary's turbulent political past and national identity.

experiences.name: Charles Bridge Sunset Stroll & Prague Food Tasting
experiences.description: Experience the magical atmosphere of the 14th-century Charles Bridge at golden hour, lined with 30 Baroque statues of saints. Follow the walk with a self-guided food tasting in the surrounding streets — try svíčková (beef sirloin), trdelník pastry, and local Czech pilsner at traditional pubs in the Lesser Town area. A perfect blend of sightseeing and culinary culture.
experiences.location: Malá Strana (Lesser Town) & Charles Bridge, Prague

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Use arrival time to clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Airport Express Bus (Line 119 to Nádraží Veleslavín, then Metro A to Hradčanská) for ~60 CZK (~€2.50) to reach your hotel in Hradčany. Check in and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely walk to explore the Hradčany neighborhood. Stroll through Hradčanské náměstí (Hradčany Square), admire the Baroque palaces and Archbishop's Palace from the outside (free), and wander down Nerudova Street with its charming Renaissance and Baroque houses. Stop at the Strahov Monastery viewpoint for a stunning panoramic view of Prague's red rooftops — completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Walk down to Malá Strana (Lesser Town) for your first evening in Prague. Explore the cobblestone streets, visit the John Lennon Wall (free), and cross the iconic Charles Bridge at dusk for magical golden-hour views. Head back toward Hradčany for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab something light at the airport or skip — you arrive at 13:00.
meals.lunch: Pick up a fresh trdelník (chimney cake, ~60 CZK) or a sandwich from a local bakery near the hotel while settling in.
meals.dinner: U Zavěšeného Kafe or a local pivnice (pub) near Malá Strana — try svíčková (beef sirloin with cream sauce) or goulash with bread dumplings for ~150–200 CZK (~€6–8). Wash it down with a local Pilsner Urquell for ~40 CZK.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Buy a 24-hour transit pass (~120 CZK) at the airport to cover all public transport for the rest of the day. September in Prague is mild (15–22°C), so a light jacket is recommended for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Start early with the crown jewel of Prague — Prague Castle (Hradský hrad). As a Hradčany resident, it's a 10-minute walk away. Purchase the Circuit B ticket (~250 CZK, ~€10) which includes St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, St. George's Basilica, and the Golden Lane. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the castle complex, the largest ancient castle in the world.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the castle, descend through the castle gardens (free in September) toward Malá Strana. Visit the stunning St. Nicholas Church in Malá Strana (~75 CZK). Cross Charles Bridge again in daylight to explore the Old Town (Staré Město). Watch the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) chime at the top of the hour on Old Town Square — free to watch from outside.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Old Town Square as the evening lights come on — a magical atmosphere. Browse the local stalls and street performers. Head to a traditional Czech beer hall for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café Louvre-style breakfast at a local café near Hradčany — coffee and pastry for ~80–100 CZK. Or grab fresh bread and cold cuts from a local potraviny (grocery store) for ~50 CZK.
meals.lunch: Lokál Dlouhááá in Old Town — a beloved Czech pub serving authentic food. Try fried cheese (smažený sýr) with tartar sauce for ~150 CZK.
meals.dinner: Pivovarský dům or Kolkovna in Old Town — hearty Czech cuisine. Roast pork knee (vepřové koleno) or beef goulash with two beers for ~250–300 CZK (~€10–12).

day_by_day.notes: Book Prague Castle tickets online in advance to skip queues. The castle opens at 9:00 AM — arrive early before tour groups arrive. Wear comfortable walking shoes — the castle grounds cover a large area with cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) — one of the best-preserved Jewish quarters in Europe. The Jewish Museum combo ticket (~550 CZK, ~€22) covers six sites including the Old Jewish Cemetery, Old-New Synagogue, and Pinkas Synagogue (with haunting Holocaust memorial inscriptions). A deeply moving and historically rich experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Vltava River to Vinohrady or Žižkov neighborhoods via tram for a local, non-touristy Prague experience. Visit the iconic Žižkov Television Tower (~250 CZK) for panoramic city views, and spot the giant crawling baby sculptures by David Černý. Explore the bohemian Vinohrady district with its Art Nouveau apartment buildings.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center for an evening walk along the Vltava riverbank. Catch a free outdoor concert or cultural event if available (check Prague.eu for September events). End the evening at a local wine bar in Vinohrady.

meals.breakfast: Café Savoy (splurge option, ~200 CZK) or a local bakery with croissant and coffee for ~80 CZK.
meals.lunch: Grab a fresh langos (fried dough with toppings, ~80–100 CZK) from a street vendor near Josefov, or a bowl of Czech soup at a nearby bistro (~80 CZK).
meals.dinner: Ambiente Pasta Fresca or a neighborhood restaurant in Žižkov — pasta or Czech dishes for ~200–250 CZK. Local craft beer from a Žižkov pub for ~50–60 CZK.

day_by_day.notes: The Jewish Quarter can be emotionally heavy — take your time. September 17 is a regular weekday so crowds should be manageable. Tram lines 5, 9, and 26 connect Josefov to Žižkov easily (~24 CZK per ride or use a day pass).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Vyšehrad Fortress — Prague's second castle, far less crowded than Prague Castle. Walk the fortress walls overlooking the Vltava River, visit the Vyšehrad Cemetery (burial place of Dvořák and Smetana), and explore the neo-Gothic Basilica of St. Peter and St. Paul (exterior free, interior ~50 CZK). The park grounds are completely free and offer stunning river views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and visit the National Museum on Wenceslas Square (Václavské náměstí) — the grand neo-Renaissance building recently renovated. Entry ~200 CZK (~€8). Stroll down Wenceslas Square, the historic boulevard where the Velvet Revolution unfolded in 1989. Visit the memorial to Jan Palach near the top of the square.
day_by_day.evening: Your last evening in Prague! Head to the Náplavka riverside embankment for the Friday farmers' market and street food stalls (open until ~20:00 in September). Grab dinner from the market stalls and enjoy the festive riverside atmosphere with locals. End with a farewell drink at a riverside bar.

meals.breakfast: Grab pastries and coffee from a local bakery near Hradčany for ~80 CZK before heading to Vyšehrad.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Vyšehrad Park — buy supplies from a local Albert or Billa supermarket (bread, cheese, charcuterie, local beer) for ~100–120 CZK total.
meals.dinner: Náplavka Farmers' Market street food — try trdelník, langos, or grilled sausages for ~100–150 CZK. A local craft beer from a market stall for ~60 CZK.

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight — tomorrow you travel to Budapest. The train or bus to Budapest departs from Prague's main station (Praha Hlavní Nádraží). Book RegioJet or Flixbus tickets in advance for ~€15–25. The journey takes approximately 6–7 hours by bus or 6.5 hours by train.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Prague to Budapest. Take the early morning RegioJet bus or train from Praha Hlavní Nádraží. Enjoy the scenic Central European countryside en route. Arrive in Budapest Keleti or Népliget station in the early afternoon. Check in to your Budapest accommodation and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Once settled, take the Metro (Line M2 or M4, ~350 HUF/~€0.90 per ride) to the city center. Start with a walk across the iconic Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) connecting Buda and Pest. Climb up to Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) on the Buda Castle Hill — the terraces are free, with spectacular panoramic views of the Danube and Parliament building.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Buda Castle district (Várnegyed) as the sun sets. Visit Matthias Church exterior (free) and soak in the fairy-tale atmosphere of the medieval streets. Descend to the Danube promenade on the Pest side for evening views of the illuminated Buda Castle and Chain Bridge.

meals.breakfast: Grab food at Prague's main station before departure — a fresh roll and coffee for ~60–80 CZK.
meals.lunch: Eat on the bus/train — bring snacks purchased from a Prague supermarket, or buy food from RegioJet's onboard bistro (~€5–8).
meals.dinner: First Budapest dinner! Try Étterem Kéhli in Buda or a local étterem (restaurant) near the castle district. Hungarian goulash soup (gulyásleves) and lángos for ~2,500–3,500 HUF (~€6–9).

day_by_day.notes: Budapest's public transport day pass costs ~2,500 HUF (~€6.50) — worth buying immediately. Validate every ticket before boarding. The Buda Castle Hill can also be reached by the historic funicular (~1,200 HUF) or free on foot via stairs. September in Budapest is warm (18–24°C) — perfect sightseeing weather.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) — one of the world's most beautiful parliament buildings. Book a guided interior tour in advance (~8,000 HUF, ~€21 for non-EU citizens; free for EU citizens with ID). Afterward, walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) and visit the Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial — a deeply moving Holocaust memorial (free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive into the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) — Budapest's largest and most atmospheric market. Browse the ground floor for fresh produce, paprika, sausages, and local cheeses. Head upstairs for folk crafts and souvenirs. Grab lunch from the market stalls. Afterward, explore the vibrant Jewish Quarter (VII District) — the largest synagogue in Europe, the Dohány Street Synagogue (~5,000 HUF, ~€13).
day_by_day.evening: Experience Budapest's legendary ruin bar scene! Head to Szimpla Kert — the original and most famous ruin bar in the Kazinczy Street area. Sunday evenings have a farmers' market in Szimpla (~16:00–20:00). Enjoy the eclectic atmosphere, local craft beers, and live music.

meals.breakfast: Café Gerbeaud on Vörösmarty Square (a Budapest institution) — coffee and pastry for ~2,500–3,500 HUF. Or a local pékség (bakery) for ~800–1,000 HUF.
meals.lunch: Great Market Hall upstairs — lángos with sour cream and cheese (~1,200 HUF), or a bowl of goulash from a market vendor (~1,500 HUF).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a restaurant in the Jewish Quarter — try Mazel Tov or Kőleves for modern Hungarian-Jewish fusion. Main courses ~3,500–5,000 HUF (~€9–13). Or eat cheaply at Szimpla Kert's food stalls (~1,500–2,500 HUF).

day_by_day.notes: Book Parliament tours online well in advance — they sell out, especially on weekends. The Great Market Hall is closed Sundays — visit the indoor section or check the Szimpla Sunday farmers' market instead. The Jewish Quarter is best explored on foot — it's compact and walkable.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a morning at the Széchenyi Thermal Baths — Budapest's most famous and grand thermal spa complex in City Park. The outdoor pools and neo-Baroque architecture are iconic. Entry with locker ~7,500 HUF (~€19). A quintessential Budapest experience and deeply relaxing after days of walking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site with the Millennium Monument and statues of Hungarian chieftains (free). Walk through Városliget (City Park) — a beautiful green space. Visit the Museum of Fine Arts (Szépművészeti Múzeum) adjacent to Heroes' Square (~3,200 HUF, ~€8) for impressive European art collections.
day_by_day.evening: Take the iconic Metro Line 1 (the oldest on the European continent, a UNESCO heritage metro) back toward the city center. Stroll along Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's grand Champs-Élysées-style boulevard — stopping to admire the Opera House exterior (free). End the evening at a local wine bar trying Hungarian Tokaj or Egri Bikavér wines.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel or a local pékség — fresh kifli (bread rolls) with butter and jam for ~600–800 HUF.
meals.lunch: Eat at the Széchenyi Baths cafeteria or bring a packed lunch to eat in City Park (~1,000–1,500 HUF from a local supermarket).
meals.dinner: Menza Restaurant on Liszt Ferenc Square — retro-style Hungarian cuisine with generous portions. Main course ~4,000–5,500 HUF (~€10–14). Or a neighborhood étterem for ~2,500–3,500 HUF.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Széchenyi Baths early (before 10:00) to avoid weekend crowds, even on Monday. Bring your own flip-flops and towel to save on rental fees (~1,000–1,500 HUF). Metro Line 1 (yellow line) runs directly from Heroes' Square to the city center — a charming heritage experience in itself.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — visit Gellért Hill (Gellért-hegy) for the best panoramic views of the entire city. Hike up for free (30–40 minutes) or take a bus to the Citadella fortress at the top. The view of the Danube, the bridges, Parliament, and Buda Castle is the finest in Budapest. Visit the Liberty Statue (Szabadság-szobor) at the summit — free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute exploration: browse the Falk Miksa Street antique shops for unique souvenirs, or return to any missed sights. Visit the Central Market Hall area one more time for last-minute food souvenirs (paprika, salami, Unicum liqueur). Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Budapest — treat yourself slightly on the last night. Head to the Buda side for a dinner with Danube views, or try a traditional Hungarian restaurant in the Belváros (Inner City). After dinner, take a final evening walk across the Chain Bridge — illuminated at night — for a perfect farewell to Eastern Europe.

meals.breakfast: Full Hungarian breakfast at a local café — eggs, cold cuts, bread, and coffee for ~2,000–2,500 HUF.
meals.lunch: Light lunch — a bowl of halászlé (Hungarian fisherman's soup) or a langos from a street vendor near the Danube for ~1,200–1,800 HUF.
meals.dinner: Arany Kaviár or Alabárdos (moderate splurge for the last night) — traditional Hungarian cuisine with atmosphere for ~6,000–8,000 HUF (~€15–20) per person. Or stay budget-friendly at a local étterem for ~3,000–4,000 HUF.

day_by_day.notes: Budapest Keleti or Budapest Liszt Ferenc Airport is well connected by Metro M4 (to Keleti) and dedicated airport bus 100E (~900 HUF, ~€2.30) from Deák Ferenc Square. Allow 60–90 minutes to reach the airport. Check your return flight time and plan accordingly. Keep some HUF for transport to the airport — card machines at some stops may be unreliable.

trip_options.title: Classic Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the Airport Express bus or taxi to your boutique hotel in Hradčany district (~30–40 min). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely first walk around Hradčany. Stroll through Hradčany Square (Hradčanské náměstí), admire the Archbishop's Palace facade, and walk along the castle walls to enjoy panoramic views of the red-rooftop city below. Visit the outer courtyards of Prague Castle (free entry) to absorb the atmosphere without rushing.
day_by_day.evening: Walk down Nerudova Street — a charming baroque lane lined with historic house signs — into Malá Strana (Lesser Town). Explore the neighborhood at dusk when the lanterns begin to glow and tourists thin out.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at the hotel or a nearby café upon settling in — no formal breakfast needed on arrival day.
meals.lunch: Light meal at a café near Hradčany Square, such as Café Poet or a local bakery — try open-faced chlebíčky sandwiches (CZK 80–150).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malostranská Beseda on Malostranské náměstí — a mid-range Czech restaurant in a historic building. Try svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) or roast duck. Budget ~CZK 350–550 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Focus on settling in and soaking up the immediate neighborhood atmosphere rather than cramming in sights.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex visit (open from 9:00). Purchase a mid-range Circuit B ticket (~CZK 250) covering St. Vitus Cathedral, Old Royal Palace, and the Basilica of St. George. Arrive early to beat crowds. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the Gothic grandeur of St. Vitus, the Bohemian Crown Jewels display, and the Romanesque basilica.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička) — a row of tiny colorful cottages once inhabited by castle guards and artisans (included in ticket). Then descend via the castle gardens or Old Castle Steps to Malá Strana. Visit the baroque Church of St. Nicholas (entry ~CZK 100) and wander Kampa Island along the Vltava riverbank.
day_by_day.evening: Cross the iconic Charles Bridge at sunset — the golden light on the 30 baroque statues is magical in September. Walk into Old Town (Staré Město) and explore the atmospheric lanes around Týn Church.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or stop at Café Louvre-style café near the castle — coffee, eggs, and toast (~CZK 150–200).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Malá Strana restaurant — try U Malého Glena or Café Savoy for a mid-range Czech lunch (CZK 200–400).
meals.dinner: Dinner in Old Town at Lokál Dlouhááá — a beloved Czech gastropub with fresh Pilsner Urquell on tap and excellent goulash or fried cheese. Budget ~CZK 300–500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Prague Castle tickets online in advance to skip queues. Wear comfortable shoes — there is significant cobblestone walking today.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Prague's Old Town (Staré Město). Start at the Old Town Square to watch the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) chime at the top of the hour. Climb the Old Town Hall Tower for panoramic views (~CZK 250). Visit the Gothic Church of Our Lady before Týn and the Baroque St. Nicholas Church in Old Town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk across to Josefov — Prague's historic Jewish Quarter. Purchase a combined Jewish Museum ticket (~CZK 500) to visit the Old Jewish Cemetery, the hauntingly beautiful Pinkas Synagogue (with names of 80,000 Holocaust victims inscribed on its walls), Maisel Synagogue, and the Spanish Synagogue with its stunning Moorish interior.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Vinohrady or Žižkov neighborhood for a local evening away from the tourist center. Browse independent shops and grab drinks at a neighborhood wine bar or craft beer pub.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café on Old Town Square — try Grand Café Orient in the Cubist House of the Black Madonna (unique architecture, CZK 150–250).
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at a local eatery in Josefov or nearby — try a bowl of goulash with bread dumplings at a traditional hospoda (~CZK 180–280).
meals.dinner: Dinner in Vinohrady at Eska (modern Czech cuisine with natural wines) or a local bistro — budget ~CZK 400–600 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Jewish Quarter is deeply moving — allow emotional space. Josefov is one of the best-preserved Jewish historic districts in Europe and should not be rushed.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Vyšehrad — Prague's second historic castle on a cliff above the Vltava, far less crowded than Prague Castle. Explore the neo-Gothic Basilica of St. Peter and St. Paul, the Vyšehrad Cemetery (burial place of Dvořák and Smetana), and the ancient Rotunda of St. Martin. Enjoy sweeping river views from the ramparts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city center and visit the National Museum on Wenceslas Square (Václavské náměstí) — recently renovated, it covers Czech natural history and national history (~CZK 250). Walk the length of Wenceslas Square, a boulevard central to Czech history including the 1989 Velvet Revolution.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert or opera. Prague is renowned for its musical heritage — check listings at the State Opera, Rudolfinum, or one of the many baroque palace concert halls. Tickets range from CZK 400–900 for mid-range seats.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh pastries and coffee from a local bakery near Hradčany before heading to Vyšehrad.
meals.lunch: Lunch near Vyšehrad at a riverside café — try Nusle area restaurants for local, non-touristy pricing (~CZK 200–350).
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Café Imperial on Na Příkopě — a stunning Art Nouveau dining room with excellent Czech-European cuisine. Budget ~CZK 450–650 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check concert schedules in advance and book tickets online. September is peak cultural season in Prague with many performances available.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take the train from Prague's Hlavní nádraží (Main Station) to Budapest Keleti. The RegioJet or Eurocity train takes approximately 6.5–7 hours with scenic countryside views through Moravia and Slovakia. Depart around 8:00–9:00 AM to arrive in Budapest by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest (~15:00–16:00). Check in to your Budapest accommodation. Take a first orientation walk along the Danube embankment near your hotel — the views of the Parliament Building across the river are among the most spectacular in Europe.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Pest side of the city. Walk through the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) if it's still open (closes ~18:00 on Saturdays) to see the stunning iron-and-glass interior and local produce. Then stroll the pedestrian Váci Street and Vörösmarty Square.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or grab food at Prague Main Station before boarding.
meals.lunch: Dining car on the train or packed lunch from a Prague deli — budget ~CZK 200–300.
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner in Budapest at Borkonyha Winekitchen (Michelin-recognized, mid-range) or Menza on Liszt Ferenc Square — try Hungarian classics like gulyás or pörkölt. Budget ~HUF 6,000–9,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book train tickets in advance on RegioJet or CD (Czech Railways) website for the best prices. The train journey through Central European countryside is a highlight in itself — bring snacks and enjoy the views.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Buda Castle Hill. Take the historic Funicular (Budavári Sikló, ~HUF 1,200 one way) from Chain Bridge up to Castle Hill. Explore the Hungarian National Gallery inside the Royal Palace (entry ~HUF 3,200), housing masterpieces of Hungarian fine art. Walk through the medieval Castle District streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom) — a stunning Gothic church with colorful Zsolnay tile roof (~HUF 2,000 entry). Walk to the adjacent Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) for the most iconic panoramic view of the Danube, Parliament, and Pest skyline. The exterior terraces are free; the upper towers have a small fee.
day_by_day.evening: Cross the Chain Bridge on foot at sunset — an unforgettable experience with the city lit up around you. Head to the Pest side for dinner in the lively Jewish Quarter (VII district) around Kazinczy Street.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a neighborhood café — try lángos (fried dough with sour cream and cheese) from a street vendor for an authentic Budapest morning (~HUF 600–900).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Castle Hill café with views — budget ~HUF 3,500–5,500 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner in the Jewish Quarter at Mazel Tov (stylish ruin-bar-style restaurant with Middle Eastern-Hungarian fusion) or Fülemüle for traditional Hungarian home cooking. Budget ~HUF 5,000–8,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Castle Hill is very walkable but hilly — wear comfortable shoes. Sunday mornings are quieter on Castle Hill before the afternoon tourist rush arrives.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building — one of the world's most beautiful legislative buildings. Book a guided interior tour in advance (~HUF 8,000 for non-EU citizens). The tour includes the domed central hall, the Hungarian Crown Jewels, and the grand staircase. Exterior views from the Danube embankment are equally spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (Dohány utcai zsinagóga) — the largest synagogue in Europe and a deeply moving Holocaust memorial site (~HUF 5,000). Afterwards, wander the Jewish Quarter's famous ruin bars district — even during the day the unique architecture of these repurposed buildings is fascinating. Visit Szimpla Kert, the original ruin bar.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a traditional Hungarian thermal bath. Visit Széchenyi Baths in City Park (the most iconic, with outdoor pools lit at night) — evening ticket ~HUF 8,500. Soak in the mineral waters under the stars in the neo-baroque palace setting.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at New York Café (splurge-worthy for the stunning Belle Époque interior — coffee and pastry ~HUF 3,000–4,500) or a simpler neighborhood café.
meals.lunch: Lunch near the Parliament at a local étterem (restaurant) — try halászlé (fisherman's soup) or stuffed peppers (~HUF 3,000–4,500).
meals.dinner: Light dinner before or after the baths — grab kürtőskalács (chimney cake) and a light meal at a nearby bistro. Budget ~HUF 3,000–5,000.

day_by_day.notes: Book Parliament tours strictly in advance online — they sell out, especially in September. Bring a swimsuit, towel, and flip-flops for the thermal baths (or rent on-site for extra cost).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) — a grand millennium monument at the end of Andrássy Avenue with statues of Hungarian tribal leaders and kings (free). Walk through City Park (Városliget) and see Vajdahunyad Castle, a fairy-tale castle complex built for the 1896 millennium exhibition. Visit the Museum of Fine Arts if time allows (~HUF 3,200).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the full length of Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's grand UNESCO-listed boulevard lined with neo-Renaissance mansions, embassies, and boutiques. Stop at the Hungarian State Opera House for a guided tour (~HUF 3,800) or simply admire its magnificent facade. Browse the upscale shops and café terraces along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening: Enjoy a sunset Danube river cruise (~HUF 5,000–7,500) to see Budapest's illuminated bridges and skyline from the water — one of the most beautiful urban night views in Europe. Then enjoy a farewell dinner in the city center.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast or a café along Andrássy Avenue.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a restaurant near City Park — try Gundel (historic upscale option for a special lunch) or a more casual nearby bistro (~HUF 4,000–7,000).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Costes Downtown or Babelfish — modern Hungarian cuisine in an elegant setting. Budget ~HUF 8,000–12,000 per person for a memorable final meal.

day_by_day.notes: If departing the next day, pack bags tonight and confirm onward transport. Book the Danube cruise in advance — September evenings are popular. The river cruise lasts about 1–1.5 hours and most include commentary on the landmarks.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from Václav Havel Airport to your boutique hotel in Hradčany district. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation stroll through the Hradčany Castle Quarter. Explore the atmospheric castle courtyards and admire St. Vitus Cathedral exterior at your own pace. Visit the charming Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička) — a row of tiny colorful houses built into the castle walls, once home to alchemists and craftsmen. Enjoy panoramic views over the red rooftops of Prague from the castle ramparts.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk across the iconic Charles Bridge, admiring the Baroque statues and the glowing city skyline. Enjoy a welcome dinner at a premium restaurant in Malá Strana to celebrate the start of your journey.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Light welcome refreshments at the hotel upon arrival, or a charcuterie and wine board at a nearby wine bar in Hradčany
meals.dinner: Dinner at Café Savoy (Malá Strana) — an elegant Art Nouveau brasserie renowned for its vaulted neo-Renaissance ceiling, exceptional Czech cuisine, and refined wine list. Try the beef tartare and svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce).

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Ask your hotel concierge to arrange a private guided castle tour for Day 2. September weather in Prague is mild (15–20°C), ideal for walking. Pack a light jacket for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Prague Castle Complex — the largest ancient castle in the world. Explore St. Vitus Cathedral interior (stunning Gothic stained glass), the Old Royal Palace (Vladislav Hall), St. George's Basilica, and the Powder Tower. Your expert guide will bring centuries of Bohemian royal history to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from the castle to the Lesser Town (Malá Strana). Visit the magnificent Baroque Church of St. Nicholas. Explore the hidden Wallenstein Garden — a formal Baroque garden with peacocks roaming freely, one of Prague's best-kept secrets. Cross Charles Bridge again in the afternoon light for photography.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert — Prague is world-famous for its chamber music performances. Many are held in historic venues such as the Lobkowicz Palace or the Church of St. Nicholas. Enjoy a pre-concert dinner in the Old Town.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at your boutique hotel — fresh pastries, cold cuts, eggs to order, and Bohemian coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Terasa U Zlaté Studně (At the Golden Well) — a Michelin-recommended restaurant with a breathtaking terrace overlooking Prague's rooftops, serving refined Czech-European cuisine
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise — a Michelin-starred restaurant offering a multi-course tasting menu inspired by historical Czech recipes, with exceptional wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book concert tickets in advance through your hotel concierge. The Lobkowicz Palace concerts are particularly intimate and prestigious. Wear smart-casual attire for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Private walking tour of Prague's Old Town (Staré Město). Visit the Old Town Square and witness the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) chime on the hour. Explore the Týn Church, the Baroque St. Nicholas Church of the Old Town, and the ornate Old Town Hall. Wander through the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) — visit the Old Jewish Cemetery and the hauntingly beautiful Pinkas Synagogue.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museum of Decorative Arts or the Jewish Museum for deeper cultural immersion. Stroll along the Pařížská Boulevard — Prague's most prestigious shopping street lined with luxury boutiques (Louis Vuitton, Hermès, Cartier). Browse for Bohemian crystal, garnets, or handcrafted souvenirs in nearby artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Evening river cruise on the Vltava River aboard a private or small-group luxury boat. Glide past illuminated bridges, the castle, and the city's glowing skyline with champagne and canapés. End the night with cocktails at a rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast followed by a traditional Czech pastry (trdelník or koláč) from an artisan bakery in the Old Town
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bellevue Restaurant — an elegant riverside restaurant with floor-to-ceiling windows framing views of Charles Bridge, serving refined European cuisine
meals.dinner: Dinner aboard the private Vltava cruise, or post-cruise dinner at Field Restaurant (Michelin-starred) — innovative Czech cuisine using hyper-local seasonal ingredients in a beautifully designed space

day_by_day.notes: The Jewish Quarter is deeply moving — allow extra time and approach with respect. Book the Vltava private cruise at least 2 days in advance through your concierge. Rooftop cocktails recommended at Cloud 9 Sky Bar & Lounge.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Český Krumlov or Kutná Hora (choose based on preference). Recommended: Kutná Hora — a UNESCO World Heritage town 1 hour from Prague. Visit the extraordinary Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church), where chandeliers and decorations are made from human bones — a macabre masterpiece. Tour the magnificent Gothic Cathedral of St. Barbara, the patron saint of miners.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Kutná Hora's medieval silver mining heritage at the Czech Museum of Silver, or return to Prague for a leisurely afternoon. If returning early, visit the Mucha Museum dedicated to Art Nouveau master Alfons Mucha, or the National Museum on Wenceslas Square.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Prague. Farewell dinner in Prague at a top-tier restaurant before preparing for tomorrow's transfer to Budapest.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kutná Hora at Pivnice Dačický — a historic restaurant in a 16th-century building serving hearty Bohemian cuisine with local Dačický beer
meals.dinner: Dinner at Alcron Restaurant (Michelin-starred) in the Art Deco Radisson Blu Alcron Hotel — famous for its exceptional seafood and intimate atmosphere with only 30 seats

day_by_day.notes: Private car or premium train service recommended for the Kutná Hora day trip. Depart by 8:30 AM to maximize time. The Ossuary requires advance ticket booking. Pack comfortable walking shoes for cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury private transfer or first-class train (Railjet) from Prague to Budapest — approximately 6.5–7 hours by train or arrange a private chauffeur-driven transfer. Enjoy the scenic Central European countryside en route. Alternatively, take a short flight (1 hour) for maximum efficiency — book business class.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest. Check in to your luxury hotel (recommended: Four Seasons Hotel Gresham Palace or Kempinski Hotel Corvinus). Freshen up and take a first walk along the iconic Chain Bridge and the Danube Promenade, soaking in views of Buda Castle across the river.
day_by_day.evening: First evening in Budapest — explore the vibrant Pest side. Stroll along Váci Street and Vörösmarty Square. Enjoy a welcome dinner at a prestigious Budapest restaurant to celebrate your arrival in the Hungarian capital.

meals.breakfast: Farewell breakfast at your Prague hotel before checkout
meals.lunch: Onboard dining on the train (first-class dining car) or a packed gourmet picnic box arranged by the Prague hotel, or stop at a café upon arrival in Budapest
meals.dinner: Dinner at Costes Restaurant — Budapest's first Michelin-starred restaurant, offering refined European cuisine with Hungarian influences in an elegant minimalist setting

day_by_day.notes: The Railjet first-class experience is scenic and comfortable — a journey in itself. Book seats well in advance. If flying, use Budapest Franz Liszt International Airport with private transfer to hotel. September is peak season in Budapest — hotel bookings must be confirmed early.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Buda Castle District (UNESCO World Heritage Site). Explore the Royal Palace, the Hungarian National Gallery, Matthias Church (a stunning Gothic masterpiece with Zsolnay ceramic tile roof), and the Fisherman's Bastion — offering some of the most spectacular panoramic views in Europe over the Danube and the Hungarian Parliament.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the Danube and cross to Pest via the Chain Bridge on foot. Visit the magnificent Hungarian Parliament Building — one of the world's most beautiful parliament buildings (book an interior guided tour in advance). Walk along the grand Andrássy Avenue (Budapest's answer to the Champs-Élysées, also UNESCO-listed) toward Heroes' Square and the Millennium Monument.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a performance at the Hungarian State Opera House — one of the most opulent opera houses in Europe, with a gilded interior rivaling Vienna's. Pre-book premium seats. Enjoy a post-opera nightcap at the hotel bar.

meals.breakfast: Grand hotel breakfast with panoramic Danube views
meals.lunch: Lunch at Halászbástya Restaurant at the Fisherman's Bastion — enjoy traditional Hungarian fish soup (halászlé) and goulash with a spectacular terrace view
meals.dinner: Pre-opera dinner at Onyx Restaurant (Michelin two-star) on Vörösmarty Square — Hungary's most celebrated fine dining destination with an extraordinary tasting menu and wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Book Parliament tours and Opera tickets weeks in advance — they sell out quickly, especially on weekends. Smart formal attire required for the Opera. The Fisherman's Bastion is magical at sunrise if you wish to visit early before crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Indulge in Budapest's legendary thermal bath culture — visit the Széchenyi Thermal Bath (the largest in Europe, housed in a stunning Neo-Baroque palace) or the more intimate and atmospheric Gellért Thermal Bath. Enjoy the mineral-rich thermal pools, steam rooms, and optional massage treatments. A quintessential Budapest experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street — the largest synagogue in Europe and the second largest in the world, a breathtaking Moorish-Byzantine masterpiece. Explore the adjacent Jewish Museum and the moving Memorial Garden. Walk through the lively Jewish Quarter (ruin bar district) — explore the eclectic Szimpla Kert ruin bar in the daytime for its unique atmosphere without the nighttime crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Danube cruise on a private luxury boat — sail past the illuminated Parliament, Chain Bridge, Buda Castle, and Gellért Hill as the city turns golden. Champagne and Hungarian wines served on board. End the evening at a rooftop bar with panoramic city views.

meals.breakfast: Light hotel breakfast before the thermal bath visit
meals.lunch: Post-bath lunch at Gerbeaud Café on Vörösmarty Square — Budapest's most historic and elegant coffeehouse since 1858, serving Hungarian pastries, Dobos torte, and light lunches
meals.dinner: Dinner at Stand Restaurant (Michelin-starred) — a modern Hungarian fine dining experience celebrating local ingredients with contemporary technique, led by acclaimed chef Tamás Széll

day_by_day.notes: Book a private massage at Gellért or Széchenyi in advance — the premium cabin treatments are exceptional. The Danube evening cruise is the highlight of Budapest — arrange through your hotel concierge for a private charter. Dress warmly for the evening boat cruise in September.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — visit the Budapest History Museum inside Buda Castle for a last dose of history, or browse the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) — a stunning iron-and-brick market hall where you can pick up premium Hungarian souvenirs: Tokaji wine, Pálinka spirits, paprika, foie gras, and Zsolnay porcelain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely farewell lunch. Last stroll along the Danube Promenade. Private luxury transfer to Budapest Franz Liszt International Airport for your departure flight. Allow ample time for premium lounge access and a relaxed send-off.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on an extraordinary 8-day journey through two of Central Europe's most magnificent capitals.

meals.breakfast: Grand final hotel breakfast — enjoy every last bite
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Borkonyha Winekitchen (Michelin-starred) — a celebrated wine-focused restaurant serving refined Hungarian dishes paired with an exceptional selection of Hungarian wines, particularly from the Tokaj and Eger regions
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for airport transfer and check-in. The Great Market Hall closes early on Sundays — confirm hours. Ship any purchased wines or fragile items via your hotel's concierge courier service to avoid luggage complications. Consider purchasing a bottle of Tokaji Aszú 5 Puttonyos as the ultimate Hungarian luxury souvenir.
